source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 13–15. The full original XML record at 14:48 includes a vowel annotation; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

key_decisions.decision: Adam includes any person; retains all three uncertain symptom terms and the priestly family. Defiling skin disease identifies the ritual category, not a modern diagnosis.
Keeps both diagnostic observations conjunctive and separates examination from the declaration; avoids calling the condition contagious.
Maintains the repeated verdict and tsaraat classification rather than treating spreading alone as a modern clinical diagnosis.
Noshenet is longstanding; the prohibition concerns provisional confinement, not permission to return to the camp. The final causal clause remains explicit.
Preserves the seemingly surprising comprehensive spread condition and the limits of visual observation; no modern explanation is supplied.
Retains the clean result for complete whitening and its repetition rather than harmonizing this with spreading cases elsewhere.
Preserves the otherwise easily omitted statement that raw flesh is unclean as well as the person's verdict.
Distinguishes shafal, lower, from amoq, deeper, rather than concealing the source's different descriptions; preserves both criteria.
Retains the source's repeated disease classification and both observations; the burnt area is not itself declared proof of impurity.
Keeps the explicit man-or-woman wording and both hair-bearing locations without inventing different rules for each sex.
Neteq receives a provisional descriptive rendering; retains thinness and yellow hair without substituting a modern named disease.
Preserves the pinned Hebrew's black hair, despite yellow hair in adjacent criteria; does not silently emend the text.
Takes hitgallach reflexively and preserves the crucial exception, the affected patch must not be shaved.
Preserves the explicit exemption from the hair check once spreading is observed, not an omitted criterion.
Retains both sexes and the source's repeated white-spot description; no modern diagnostic name is added.
Uses a provisional description for bohaq without diagnosing vitiligo or claiming that clean means medically harmless.
Preserves the male case and baldness as clean; back of the head reflects the contrast with frontal baldness in verse 41.
Keeps the emphatic declaration and last location clause separate without adding an explicit causal connective absent in Hebrew.
Preserves visible distress markers and the doubled cry; upper lip renders safam without turning the command into a modern protective mask rule.
Retains repetition, duration, isolation and compulsory outside-camp dwelling; does not soften the exclusion or invent a medical rationale.
Uses growth for material tsaraat while explicitly linking the human and material category in the apparatus; preserves both fabrics.
Keeps warp and weft distinct with vocabulary support, and preserves raw leather and manufactured articles.
Preserves every listed material and both colors; does not identify the growth as a known mold species.
Keeps the full material list and manufacturing clause; destructive renders mammeret without the modern clinical implications of malignant.
Preserves unchanged appearance as decisive despite no spread. Pehetet and the reused baldness terms are uncertain; corroding and back/front are provisional and noted.
Renders torah as instructions and keeps all material classes and the two possible priestly outcomes in the closing summary.
